To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
first person viewpoint is important for visuo tactile integration (and thus for the sense of body ownership) for the lower limbs.

the visuo tactile congruency effect and the subjective sense of body ownership are both significantly enhanced when participants are shown a virtual leg from the first person viewpoint compared to the third person viewpoint.
the visuo tactile congruency effect as well as the strength of leg ownership is significantly increased for a first person visuo perspective compared to a third person visuo perspective.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of visuospatial viewpoint in the integration of visuotactile information and the sense of body ownership.
how the brain processes and integrates multisensory information from our body, and how the resulting bodily signals are integrated with the visual information from our body.
the integration of visuotactile information and the sense of body ownership.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the visuo tactile CCE and the sense of leg body ownership is significantly boosted by a first person visuo perspective.

the visuo tactile CCE and leg ownership are both significantly boosted by the first person visuospatial viewpoint, and that the visuo-tactile CCE is only present in the conditions when the visual stimuli are perceived as a leg. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2019 APA, all rights reserved)
the visuo tactile congruency is stronger for first person visuo viewpoint and that leg ownership is also stronger for first person view point, however, the effect on leg ownership is less clear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the visuo tactile interaction is enhanced if the visual stimuli are seen from the first person viewpoint and if the stimuli are anatomically similar to the body part that is stimulated.
the integration of visuotactile stimuli and the resulting sense of body ownership is enhanced by the visual viewpoint from where the stimuli are presented.
the visuo tactile interaction is stronger when the body is perceived from the first person viewpoint.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the sense of leg body ownership depends on the visual top down signal of visuo spatial perspective and that the visuo tactile crossmodal congruence effect is a valid measure for visuo tactile integration.
first person visuo tactile integration is a crucial component of body ownership and that the first person viewpoint boosts this visuo tactile integration.
first person viewpoint is important for the integration of visual and tactile signals and the subjective experience of ownership.
